<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from app/config.py and .env.example. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting is read from the environment - a `.env` file next to the
compose file, or your Docker manager's stack environment. Most can also be
changed on the dashboard's [Settings page](/container-doctor/guides/settings/); a variable
set in the environment always wins. Empty is the same as unset.

- **Secret**: never shown by value, and never saved from the Settings page.
- **Environment only**: read before the database opens, so the Settings page
  cannot change it.
- **Applies on restart**: read once at start; a change takes effect when the
  doctor restarts.
- **`off` turns it off**: on by default; set `off` (or `none` for a list) to
  disable it.

## Build and mode

### DOCTOR_MODE

- `observe` - diagnose and notify, never touch anything   <- start here
- `suggest` - propose an action, wait for you to approve it in the dashboard
- `auto` - apply allowed actions without asking

**Default:** `observe` · **One of:** `observe`, `suggest`, `auto`

### DOCTOR_POLL_INTERVAL

Poll interval: from the start of one poll to the next.

**Default:** `30` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_POLL_CONCURRENCY

Containers read at once during a poll. `docker stats` takes a second or two per container, so one at a time made a poll of 30 run over a minute.

**Default:** `6` · **Type:** whole number · **Applies on restart**

### DOCKER_HOST

The Docker endpoint: the socket proxy, never the raw socket. The compose file sets it from DOCTOR_DOCKER_HOST.

**Default:** `tcp://doctor-socket-proxy:2375` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_REQUIRE_OPT_IN

Opt-in only: on watches only containers labelled doctor.enable=true; off watches every container except doctor.enable=false.

**Default:** `off` · **Type:** on / off

## Deployment

### DOCTOR_DOCKER_MANAGER

In words, for the diagnosis, the hand-off brief and the Settings page's labels; neither changes what the doctor does. Both optional. The Docker manager's name: Portainer, Coolify, Komodo, Dockge...

**Default:** `unset`

### DOCTOR_DEPLOY_METHOD

How a change reaches the host.

**Default:** `unset`

### DOCTOR_HOST_KIND

What the doctor runs on. auto reads it from the kernel: a Synology says so, and then DSM's own md0/md1 system arrays are not called degraded. Set synology or generic to override. The name is what diagnoses and the Host page call it; empty says "the host".

**Default:** `auto` · **One of:** `auto`, `synology`, `generic`

### DOCTOR_HOST_NAME

The machine itself. auto tells a Synology NAS from any other Linux by its kernel; synology keeps DSM's md0/md1 system arrays from reading as degraded and uses its names for drives and pools. The name is what the host is called in diagnoses and on the Host page - empty says "the host".

**Default:** `unset`

## Model

### DOCTOR_LLM_PROVIDER

Set DOCTOR_LLM_PROVIDER=openai and point at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Verify it in one command before you rely on it: docker compose exec container-doctor python -m app.selftest  Google Gemini - free tier, no card. See the README for the privacy caveat.

**Default:** `anthropic` · **One of:** `anthropic`, `openai` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_MODEL

OpenRouter `:free` variants cost nothing but are rate-limited hard (20 req/min; 50/day under $10 of credits, 1000/day above).

**Default:** `claude-opus-5`

### DOCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL

OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, vLLM, ...).

**Default:** `unset`

### ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

Anthropic API key. Without it the doctor still detects incidents and shows them in the dashboard - it just cannot explain them.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_OPENAI_API_KEY

OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, vLLM, ...).

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_EFFORT

Low | medium | high | xhigh | max - how hard the model thinks per incident. Only applies to Anthropic models; ignored elsewhere.

**Default:** `medium` · **One of:** `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`

### DOCTOR_LLM_TEMPERATURE

Reasoning models reject `temperature` (GPT-6 Luna does at any reasoning effort above `none`). The request drops it automatically if the vendor complains; set -1 to never send it and skip the extra round trip.

**Default:** `0.2` · **Type:** number

## Cost

### DOCTOR_PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK

USD per million tokens, so the spend meter works for a non-Anthropic vendor. Leave at -1 to price known Anthropic models from the built-in table and treat everything else as free. Set both to 0 to say "this really is free".

**Default:** `-1` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK

USD per million tokens. Unset prices Anthropic models from a built-in table and counts anything else as free - hence the call cap above.

**Default:** `-1` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DAILY_USD_BUDGET

Hard stop for the day once this much has been spent. 0 disables the cap.

**Default:** `1` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DAILY_CALL_LIMIT

Hard stop after this many calls today. This is the cap that matters on a free tier, where the dollar meter reads zero all day. 0 disables it.

**Default:** `0` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_DIAGNOSIS_CACHE_HOURS

Identical failures reuse a stored diagnosis for this many hours (no API call).

**Default:** `6` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LLM_LOG_DAYS

Every request as it was sent, on the LLM page, for this many days. 0 keeps none; the daily spend totals are kept either way.

**Default:** `14` · **Type:** whole number

## Detection

### DOCTOR_CPU_THRESHOLD

Share of the WHOLE host's CPU, not of a single core.

**Default:** `85` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_MEM_THRESHOLD

Share of the container's memory limit (or of host RAM when no limit is set).

**Default:** `90` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_RESOURCE_BREACH_POLLS

Consecutive polls a breach must persist for, so one backup spike is quiet.

**Default:** `4` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_RESTART_LOOP_COUNT

Consecutive polls a breach must persist for, so one backup spike is quiet.

**Default:** `3` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_RESTART_LOOP_WINDOW_MINUTES

Consecutive polls a breach must persist for, so one backup spike is quiet.

**Default:** `15` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LOG_LINES

Consecutive polls a breach must persist for, so one backup spike is quiet.

**Default:** `120` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LOG_MAX_AGE_MINUTES

Ignore log lines older than this. A quiet container's `tail` reaches back as far as it has been running - Docmost's Postgres was serving FATAL lines from 2025 to a poll in 2026, which read as a live failure.

**Default:** `60` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LOG_ERROR_BURST

Lines matching DOCTOR_LOG_ERROR_PATTERN by wording.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR_BURST

Lines the app itself marked ERROR. Higher, because one ERROR line is weaker evidence than "no space left on device".

**Default:** `10` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_LOG_FATAL_THRESHOLD

A single FATAL / CRITICAL line opens an incident on its own.

**Default:** `1` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_DEPLOY_SETTLE_MINUTES

Redeploys. A stop that Docker announced with a signal (docker stop, Compose, a Docker manager) is not a crash, and a container that exits and is replaced within DOCTOR_DIE_GRACE_SECONDS was redeployed. For DOCTOR_DEPLOY_SETTLE_MINUTES after any redeploy, errors other containers log while it restarts do not count, and a failing health check waits. 0 turns the window off.

**Default:** `3` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DIE_GRACE_SECONDS

A nonzero exit nobody asked for waits this long before it is a crash: if the container was replaced meanwhile, it was a redeploy.

**Default:** `30` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_LOG_IGNORE_PATTERN

Log lines to never count, host-wide. Prefer the per-container label `doctor.ignore_log` - noise is usually one container's habit.

**Default:** `unset`

### DOCTOR_DISK_PATHS

Free space is a property of the filesystem, so /data reports all of the volume it lives on without mounting it. To watch a second volume, mount a small directory on it read-only (never the volume root) and add it here.

**Default:** `none` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_DISK_THRESHOLD

A storage host that is simply well used sits high for years; 90% pestered about a disk with terabytes free.

**Default:** `95` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DISK_CRITICAL

How often a disk's free space is recorded for the fill forecast.

**Default:** `95` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DISK_FORECAST_DAYS

Where the same condition stops being a warning. Was hard-coded at 95. How far back the fill-rate is fitted, and how close to full is worth saying something about. A percentage says how full; these say whether it is going anywhere.

**Default:** `21` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_DISK_FORECAST_CRITICAL_DAYS

Where the same condition stops being a warning. Was hard-coded at 95. How far back the fill-rate is fitted, and how close to full is worth saying something about. A percentage says how full; these say whether it is going anywhere.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_DISK_TREND_WINDOW_DAYS

Where the same condition stops being a warning. Was hard-coded at 95. How far back the fill-rate is fitted, and how close to full is worth saying something about. A percentage says how full; these say whether it is going anywhere.

**Default:** `14` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_MDSTAT_PATH

The kernel's account of every md array. off turns the RAID check off.

**Default:** `/proc/mdstat` · **`off` turns it off**

### DOCTOR_SYSFS_PATH

Where the arrays' layout, scrub results and per-disk errors are read from. Docker mounts the host's /sys read-only; off skips it.

**Default:** `/sys` · **Applies on restart** · **`off` turns it off**

### DOCTOR_RAID_ERRORS_PER_DAY

How many newly corrected read errors in a day turn a drive's warning critical. The first one is always a warning; this is "and it is getting worse". md itself fails a member at 20 corrected errors that come faster than its hourly halving drains them; 0 never escalates.

**Default:** `10` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_RAID_ERRORS_DAYS

How long a drive's newly corrected read errors keep its warning up. md's own count only goes back to 0 on a reboot, so without a window a drive that had a bad day would warn until the next one.

**Default:** `7` · **Type:** whole number

## Host

### DOCTOR_PROC_PATH

The host itself (Host page). Read from /proc, which is system-wide; off turns it off. An incident opens when a condition lasts DOCTOR_HOST_BREACH_POLLS.

**Default:** `/proc` · **Applies on restart** · **`off` turns it off**

### DOCTOR_HOST_MEM_AVAILABLE_PCT

Below this share of memory available (the kernel's MemAvailable, which counts reclaimable cache) the host is about to swap or OOM-kill.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_HOST_SWAP_IN_PER_S

Pages read back from swap per second. Swap being used is normal - Linux, DSM especially, parks idle pages there - swap being read back steadily is not.

**Default:** `256` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_HOST_LOAD_PER_CORE

The 5-minute load average per CPU. Linux load counts processes waiting on disks as well as on CPU, so it reads high during a scrub.

**Default:** `2` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_HOST_IOWAIT_PCT

Share of CPU time spent waiting on disks.

**Default:** `40` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_HOST_TEMP_C

Pages read back from swap per second. Swap being used is normal - Linux, DSM especially, parks idle pages there - swap being read back steadily is not.

**Default:** `80` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_HOST_BREACH_POLLS

Consecutive polls a host breach must last: ten is five minutes at the default interval, so a backup's burst of I/O wait stays quiet.

**Default:** `10` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_HOST_SAMPLE_MINUTES

One stored point per this many minutes, for the Host page's charts.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** whole number

## Internet and DNS

### DOCTOR_NET_CHECK_SECONDS

Internet and DNS (Network page), checked from the doctor's container.

**Default:** `60` · **Type:** whole number · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_NET_TCP_TARGETS

Addresses, not names: reaching them says the line works, whatever DNS does.

**Default:** `1.1.1.1:443, 9.9.9.9:443` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_NET_DNS_NAMES

Resolved the way containers resolve names.

**Default:** `cloudflare.com, github.com` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_NET_DNS_SERVERS

Your own DNS servers, each checked on its own: ip or ip:port.

**Default:** `none` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_NET_HTTP_URLS

DNS servers asked directly - a Pi-hole, AdGuard, the router - as ip or ip:port. Empty by default: which ones exist is the network's business.

**Default:** `https://www.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_NET_FAIL_ROUNDS

Rounds in a row a check must fail before an incident opens, and pass before it closes.

**Default:** `3` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_NET_TIMEOUT

Internet and DNS, checked from the doctor's container every this many seconds. 0 turns the checks off. "none" empties any of the lists.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** number

## Drive health

### DOCTOR_SMART_URL

The SMART sidecar's metrics page. off turns drive health off.

**Default:** `http://doctor-smart:9633/metrics` · **`off` turns it off**

### DOCTOR_SMART_TEMP_C

The SMART sidecar's metrics page. off turns drive health off.

**Default:** `55` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_SMART_NVME_TEMP_C

The SMART sidecar's metrics page. off turns drive health off.

**Default:** `70` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_SMART_WEAR_PCT

Share of an SSD's rated write endurance used before it is worth a word.

**Default:** `90` · **Type:** number

## Remediation

### DOCTOR_AUTO_ACTIONS

Auto-applies: only in auto mode.

**Default:** `restart_container` · **Any of:** `none`, `notify_only`, `restart_container`, `stop_container`, `prune_images`

### DOCTOR_MIN_CONFIDENCE

- `observe` - diagnose and notify, never touch anything   <- start here
- `suggest` - propose an action, wait for you to approve it in the dashboard
- `auto` - apply allowed actions without asking

**Default:** `0.75` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_MAX_ACTIONS_PER_CONTAINER_PER_HOUR

Circuit breakers: at most this many actions on one container, and on the whole host, in any hour. doctor.max_actions_per_hour tightens the first.

**Default:** `3` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_MAX_ACTIONS_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR

Circuit breakers: at most this many actions on one container, and on the whole host, in any hour. doctor.max_actions_per_hour tightens the first.

**Default:** `10` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_ACTION_COOLDOWN_MINUTES

Blocks re-running the same action for the same fingerprint.

**Default:** `30` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_VERIFY_DELAY

Seconds to wait after an action before checking whether it actually helped.

**Default:** `45` · **Type:** whole number

## Incident lifecycle

### DOCTOR_INCIDENT_DEDUP_HOURS

How long a recurrence folds into the open incident instead of opening a new one. Measured from when it was last seen, so a condition that keeps firing stays a single incident for as long as it lasts.

**Default:** `24` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_AUTO_RESOLVE_HOURS

Resolve an incident whose condition has not re-fired for this long. 0 is off. Kinds that suppress their own re-alerts are excluded - see Store.auto_resolve_stale.

**Default:** `12` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_RETENTION_DAYS

Read GitHub release notes for images with a newer version, to link them and flag the ones that mention breaking changes. One unauthenticated request per such image per check.

**Default:** `30` · **Type:** whole number

## Access

### DOCTOR_OIDC_ISSUER

--- OIDC --------------------------------------------------------------- Issuer base URL, e.g. https://id.example.com. Empty disables OIDC.

**Default:** `unset` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_OIDC_CLIENT_ID

The client ID registered with the provider for the doctor.

**Default:** `unset` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_PUBLIC_URL

The doctor's own public base URL; the redirect URI is derived from it and must match what the provider has registered exactly.

**Default:** `unset` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_WEB_PASSWORD

Protects the dashboard. Approvals and manual actions are disabled until this is set, because the dashboard can restart containers.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET

The client ID registered with the provider for the doctor.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS

Empty means any account the provider authenticates.

**Default:** `none` · **Type:** comma-separated list · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_SESSION_HOURS

How long a session survives unused. In use, it lasts as long as the provider keeps renewing its tokens.

**Default:** `12` · **Type:** whole number · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_SESSION_SECRET

Signs the session cookie. Unset means a random one per start, which logs everyone out on restart.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_WEB_PASSWORD_FALLBACK

Once OIDC is configured the password is refused by default, so there is one way in. Turn this on to keep it as a way back in when the provider itself is the thing that is broken.

**Default:** `off` · **Type:** on / off · **Applies on restart**

## Briefing

### DOCTOR_BRIEFING

The summary at the top of the dashboard. Needs an LLM; off leaves the deterministic facts in its place.

**Default:** `on` · **Type:** on / off

### DOCTOR_BRIEFING_MODEL

A smaller model is plenty for three lines of summary. Empty: DOCTOR_MODEL.

**Default:** `unset`

### DOCTOR_BRIEFING_REFRESH_MINUTES

How often a section may be rewritten when its facts change without its level changing. A new critical incident does not wait for this.

**Default:** `15` · **Type:** whole number

## Classifier

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER

A decision model's second opinion on judgement signals (error bursts, health checks, CPU/memory) before they become incidents. off | shadow | on. shadow records verdicts and changes nothing - run it that way first.

**Default:** `off` · **One of:** `off`, `shadow`, `on`

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_PROVIDER

Openrouter: a decision model via OpenRouter's Decisions API (Jev). chat: the diagnosis's own model; uncalibrated, so it never hides anything.

**Default:** `openrouter` · **One of:** `openrouter`, `chat`

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_MODEL

Pinned rather than -latest, so verdicts do not drift under you.

**Default:** `typesafe/jev-1.13`

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_URL

The Decisions API endpoint the openrouter backend calls.

**Default:** `https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions`

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_API_KEY

An OpenRouter key. Give it its own credit limit on openrouter.ai. Unset: the diagnosis's DOCTOR_OPENAI_API_KEY, if that is an OpenRouter one.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_SUPPRESS_AT

Likely-noise probability at or above which a signal opens no incident (on).

**Default:** `0.9` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_DAILY_CALLS

Its own caps, separate from the diagnosis's.

**Default:** `500` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_DAILY_USD

Probability of noise at or above which a signal opens no incident.

**Default:** `0.1` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_MAX_PER_MINUTE

A host coming back up fires everything at once; past this, the rules decide alone until the minute is over.

**Default:** `10` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_CACHE_HOURS

A host coming back up fires everything at once; past this, the rules decide alone until the minute is over.

**Default:** `6` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_TIMEOUT

A host coming back up fires everything at once; past this, the rules decide alone until the minute is over.

**Default:** `5` · **Type:** number

## Updates

### DOCTOR_IMAGE_CHECK_HOURS

How often to ask the registries what they currently publish. The doctor never pulls itself - the socket proxy denies POST /images - but a new build can be redeployed from the dashboard through the deploy workflow.

**Default:** `12` · **Type:** whole number · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_UPDATE_COOLDOWN_DAYS

A newer version counts once it has been on Docker Hub this many days - match a Dependabot cooldown (or Renovate's minimumReleaseAge), so the dashboard lists what it will propose rather than running days ahead of it. 0 reports every release at once.

**Default:** `3` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_RELEASE_NOTES

Read GitHub release notes for images with a newer version, to link them and flag the ones that mention breaking changes. One unauthenticated request per such image per check.

**Default:** `on` · **Type:** on / off

### DOCTOR_GITHUB_TOKEN

Redeploy a stack from the Updates page when its image has a new build. The doctor runs a GitHub Actions workflow in the repository the stacks are deployed from, which redeploys the stack - see examples/redeploy-workflow.yml for what it must accept. A fine-grained token on that repository only, with Actions: read and write, and Contents: read. Unset, the page only reports.

**Default:** `unset` · **Secret**

### DOCTOR_BUILD

Stamped into the image by CI. "dev" means a local build.

**Default:** `dev` · **Environment only**

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_MAX_STATE_CHARS

Roughly 3,000 tokens: the evidence without the tail of a long log.

**Default:** `12000` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_CLASSIFIER_PRICE_PER_MTOK

Jev's input price; its output is free. Used when OpenRouter does not report the cost itself.

**Default:** `0.042` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_DATA_DIR

Where the database lives inside the container; mount a volume here.

**Default:** `/data` · **Environment only**

### DOCTOR_DISK_SAMPLE_MINUTES

How often a disk's free space is recorded for the fill forecast.

**Default:** `60` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_IGNORE_CONTAINERS

Comma-separated container names the doctor must never look at or touch.

**Default:** `none` · **Type:** comma-separated list

### DOCTOR_LLM_MAX_RETRIES

Retries on 429 / 5xx, honouring Retry-After. Free tiers rate-limit hard.

### DOCTOR_LLM_TIMEOUT

Free tiers rate-limit hard (Gemini free: 10/minute); retry rather than lose the diagnosis.

**Default:** `180` · **Type:** number

### DOCTOR_LOG_ERROR_PATTERN

A log line matching this counts as an error, whatever its level says.

**Default:** `(?i)\b(fatal|panic|traceback|segfault|out of memory|oomkill|connection refused|no such host|permission denied|disk full|no space left|deadlock|unhandled exception)\b`

### DOCTOR_LOG_LEVEL

Stamped into the image by CI. "dev" means a local build.

### DOCTOR_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS

Cap on the tokens one diagnosis may answer with.

**Default:** `4000` · **Type:** whole number

### DOCTOR_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM

The ID token claim holding the user's groups, for DOCTOR_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS.

**Default:** `groups` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_OIDC_SCOPES

Scopes requested at sign-in, space-separated.

**Default:** `openid profile email groups` · **Applies on restart**

### DOCTOR_SELF_NAME

The doctor's own container name: it never diagnoses or acts on itself.

**Default:** `container-doctor`

### DOCTOR_SETTINGS_EDITABLE

Settings can be changed on the Settings page by anyone who can sign in; a variable set here always overrides what was saved there. false makes the page read-only.

**Default:** `on` · **Type:** on / off · **Environment only**

### DOCTOR_WEB_HOST

Address and port the dashboard listens on inside the container.

**Default:** `0.0.0.0` · **Environment only**

### DOCTOR_WEB_PORT

Address and port the dashboard listens on inside the container.

**Default:** `8080` · **Type:** whole number · **Environment only**

### DOCTOR_WEB_USER

The user name that password signs in as.

**Default:** `doctor` · **Applies on restart**

## Read by the compose file

These never reach the doctor: the reference compose file reads them itself.

### DOCTOR_PROXY_ALLOW_POST

Set to 0 to close the socket proxy's only write route. The doctor then physically cannot restart anything, whatever mode it is in. (This maps to ALLOW_RESTARTS on the proxy; the global POST gate is always off, which is what keeps /containers/create - arbitrary host mounts - out of reach.)


### DOCTOR_SMART_DEVICES

Drive health from the doctor-smart sidecar (Storage page). "auto" finds the drives; or list their device files, space or comma separated. Give SATA drives their type, /dev/sata1;sat, or smartctl may read a WD as SCSI.


### DOCTOR_DATA_VOLUME

Where the database lives on the host and who owns it - read by the compose file itself.


### DOCTOR_UID

Where the database lives on the host and who owns it - read by the compose file itself.


### DOCTOR_GID

Where the database lives on the host and who owns it - read by the compose file itself.


### DOCTOR_PORT

Read by compose.example.yaml itself: the dashboard's port on the host, and where the database lives there and who owns it.


### DOCTOR_IMAGE_TAG

Pin to a specific published image instead of tracking latest, e.g. a sha-<commit> tag from ghcr.io, to roll back or freeze a deploy.


### TZ

Pin to a specific published image instead of tracking latest, e.g. a sha-<commit> tag from ghcr.io, to roll back or freeze a deploy.
